question.latex: A $0.5\text{ kg}$ mass is in contact against the inner wall of a cylindrical drum of radius $4\text{ m}$ rotating about its vertical axis. The minimum rotational speed of the drum to enable the mass to remain stuck to the wall $without falling$ is $5\text{ rad/s}$. The coefficient of friction between the drum's inner wall surface and mass is _______ . $Take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$$
question.unicode: A 0.5text{ kg} mass is in contact against the inner wall of a cylindrical drum of radius 4text{ m} rotating about its vertical axis. The minimum rotational speed of the drum to enable the mass to remain stuck to the wall without falling is 5text{ rad/s}. The coefficient of friction between the drum's inner wall surface and mass is _______ . Take g = 10text{ m/s}²
question.plainText: A 0.5text{ kg} mass is in contact against the inner wall of a cylindrical drum of radius 4text{ m} rotating about its vertical axis. The minimum rotational speed of the drum to enable the mass to remain stuck to the wall without falling is 5text{ rad/s}. The coefficient of friction between the drum's inner wall surface and mass is _______ . Take g = 10text{ m/s}^2

explanation.latex:
For the mass to remain stuck without falling, the upward static friction must balance the downward gravitational force: $f = mg$.
The normal force provided by the wall is the centripetal force: $N = m \omega^2 r$.
The maximum static friction is $f_{max} = \mu N = \mu m \omega^2 r$.
Setting $mg = \mu m \omega^2 r$, the mass $m$ cancels out.
$\mu = \frac{g}{\omega^2 r} = \frac{10}{5^2 \times 4} = \frac{10}{25 \times 4} = \frac{10}{100} = 0.1$.
